title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — notable papers in the 9 November 2026 batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this inferred relevance-and-evidence ranking is not a popularity ranking, and arXiv covers only part of biomedical preprinting, with much clinical and experimental work appearing on bioRxiv or medRxiv.

sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: Daily batch 2026-11-09: eleven notable biology and biomedical papers, led by pathology-scale demographic mapping, coupled RNA/chromatin trajectories, and bias-aware GWAS. arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance-and-evidence ranking from incomplete biomedical coverage.

sections.title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
sections.abstract: An analysis of 1.3 million H&E slides from 257,322 patients across 25 organs found that models could recover sex, age group, and self-reported race from histology, with performance varying by organ and demographic label.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a systematic map of demographic-associated information in routine histopathology and identify possible implications for shortcut learning; their proposed tissue/context explanations remain hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: Predictability does not identify its biological or social source. This is a retrospective single-health-system analysis, and diagnosis-based grouping does not substitute for external replication or causal interpretation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Highest direct biomedical relevance and cohort scale in this batch; 1.3 million slides, 257,322 patients, 25 organs, and 69 organ-demographic combinations are reported by the authors.

sections.title: Synchronized Optimal Transport Reconstructs Coupled Transcriptomic and Chromatin Dynamics
sections.abstract: COATI jointly models time-varying RNA and ATAC trajectories in separate state spaces and is evaluated on synthetic data and four developmental datasets, including held-out-stage reconstruction and lineage analyses.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors say synchronized unbalanced optimal transport improves held-out population reconstruction and preserves chromatin heterogeneity and developmental lineage relationships.
sections.unique_caveat: Trajectories are inferred from destructive snapshots, not tracked individual cells; results depend on a pretrained RNA-to-ATAC map, and agreement with held-out distributions alone cannot establish the true lineage path.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Strong fit to RNA/genomics focus; authors report four developmental datasets, held-out-stage tests, and agreement of inferred lineage responses with independent CRISPR perturbation and epigenetic results.

sections.title: Navigating Selection Bias in Genome-wide Association Studies (GWAS)
sections.abstract: This methods review organizes ten ways to diagnose or correct GWAS selection bias by data availability and selection mechanism, with R implementations for nine methods and simulated examples.
sections.claimed_contribution: The review offers a decision framework for diagnosing or correcting participation, case-control, index-event, sex-differential, and survival-related selection bias.
sections.unique_caveat: It is a methods synthesis, not a new population-scale validation of the methods; each correction remains conditional on its assumptions and required data.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Broad relevance to biobank and genetic inference; the authors compare ten methods, state their assumptions and data needs, and provide code plus worked simulated examples.
sections.announcement_type: new submission, cross-listed in genomics and quantitative biology

sections.title: Dual-energy cardiac DSA imaging using a dual-layer flat-panel detector: in vivo validation study
sections.abstract: A dual-energy material-decomposition method using a dual-layer detector is evaluated with simulations and preliminary in-vivo swine cardiac angiography, with the authors reporting improved vessel contrast and reduced scatter effects.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose temporally subtracted low/high-energy projections with penalized-likelihood decomposition to improve iodine-specific cardiac vessel imaging without explicit scatter correction.
sections.unique_caveat: Preliminary animal validation is not human clinical evidence; residual scatter may remain under larger motion, and the current method decomposes soft tissue and iodine rather than multiple materials.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct medical-imaging validation: Monte Carlo simulations and in-vivo swine experiments on a clinical DSA system; the authors report over 80% lower scatter impact in simulation.

sections.title: Personalized health coaching via coachable health age and counterfactual wearable trajectories
sections.abstract: The authors combine a wearable-derived health-age metric with a model trained on over 2.2 million person-weeks to forecast responses to lifestyle changes and generate counterfactual coaching plans, evaluated across three cohorts and by expert reviewers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved prognostic discrimination over age, sex, and BMI, multi-week response forecasts, and greater expert preference for counterfactual-grounded plans.
sections.unique_caveat: Forecast accuracy and expert review do not show that the plans change behavior or health outcomes; a prospective intervention study is not reported in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper reports three cohorts (N=2,780; 22,748; and 1,464), a SensorWM model pretrained on roughly 100,000 participants, and blinded coach/clinician review of generated plans.

sections.title: Smart Spectral Doppler Ultrasound Imaging using Motion Tracking based on Wide-beam transmission and Neural Networks: Preliminary Results
sections.abstract: The proposed single-transmit wide-beam Doppler method tracks vessel motion and updates the sample volume; simulations and in-vivo carotid-artery and hepatic-vein demonstrations report improved spectral signal-to-noise under tissue motion.
sections.claimed_contribution: Wide-beam transmission is intended to preserve pulse-repetition frequency while a lightweight tracker follows motion and repositions the Doppler sample volume.
sections.unique_caveat: The in-vivo evidence is limited to two demonstrations; performance across patients, pathologies, and routine clinical workflows is not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors report Field II simulations plus in-vivo demonstrations in two vessels, with 9.3 dB and 4.5 dB spectral-SNR gains respectively.

sections.title: SmartBloch-Agent: An Agentic Framework for Automated MRI Sequence Design and Optimization
sections.abstract: SmartBloch-Agent uses an AI agent and an in-house Bloch simulator to turn natural-language imaging objectives into MRI sequence designs, simulations, reconstructions, and optimization feedback.
sections.claimed_contribution: The framework links sequence construction, physical simulation, parameter search, reconstruction, and evaluation into an agent-driven research loop.
sections.unique_caveat: Reported evidence is computational; scanner deployment and independent validation on acquired patient data are not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across medical physics, AI, and imaging; the authors report automated experiments across varied objectives and improved parameter-estimation and quantitative-reconstruction metrics.

sections.title: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction
sections.abstract: KineCouple uses substrate-conditioned cross-attention over residue features to predict enzyme kcat and Km, reporting small pooled out-of-fold improvements over reproduced CataPro results.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors condition residue-level aggregation on substrate features while keeping the ProtT5 and MolT5 encoders frozen.
sections.unique_caveat: Reported metric gains are very small; repeated-run variability and matched controls are needed, and attention weights do not establish physical catalytic contacts.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct enzyme-kinetics relevance and a benchmark comparison; the abstract reports RMSE/Pearson improvements on both kcat and Km tasks.
sections.announcement_type: new submission, cross-listed to quantitative biology

sections.title: Pangenome Peeling: Decomposing Weighted Adjacencies into Path-Forest Genomes
sections.abstract: The authors define an inverse pangenome problem that reconstructs constituent linear genomes from weighted adjacency graphs and compare two algorithms on simulated data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The maximum-spanning-tree path decomposition reportedly recovers simulated constituent genomes more faithfully than sequential edge addition as genome size grows.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is simulation-based; performance on real, noisy pangenome graphs and ancestral genomes remains unshown.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct genomics application, with a formal problem definition, lower-bound result, and simulation comparison using genome similarity and matching criteria.

sections.title: Protein B-factor modeling with local magnitude
sections.abstract: A local geometric descriptor for protein structures modestly improves B-factor prediction across protein benchmarks while reducing feature-extraction cost for large structures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce nearest-neighbor local magnitude features and report lower asymptotic factorization cost than global magnitude for large structures.
sections.unique_caveat: Predictive gains are modest and experiments use a single-seed configuration; faster extraction is not universal for small proteins.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Protein-focused method with 364 proteins in fitting analyses and 345 in blind prediction across three validation protocols; the reported local-feature gains are consistent but small.

sections.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Annealing for Protein Side-Chain Optimization: A Feasibility Study
sections.abstract: A hybrid annealer is compared with Gurobi on 40 side-chain optimization instances derived from 20 experimentally determined protein structures, with the authors reporting competitive or lower-energy solutions on larger instances.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that side-chain optimization is a suitable binary-quadratic problem for testing hybrid annealing and report that it reaches certified optima when available.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a feasibility study, not experimental protein-design validation; the authors call for comparisons with heuristics tailored to side-chain optimization.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct computational protein-design task, 40 instances from 20 structures, and comparisons with a commercial solver at multiple runtime budgets.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: The batch combines cross-modal RNA/ATAC and genome-analysis work with a large pathology study. Medical imaging papers report different evidence levels, from animal in-vivo demonstration to simulation-only MRI sequence design. Protein papers address kinetic prediction, B-factor modeling, and side-chain optimization; they remain computational results rather than experimental validation.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Follow-up work suggested by the selected papers includes external and blinded pathology replication with confounder-aware analyses; denser time points, lineage tracing, and map-sensitivity tests for COATI; repeated-run and matched-compute tests for enzyme/protein predictions; real noisy graph evaluation for pangenome reconstruction; and prospective clinical/outcome validation for imaging and wearable coaching claims.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The batch's strongest work combines computational methods with large datasets or explicit validation, but evidence ranges from retrospective cohorts and simulations to animal imaging. None of these preprints alone supports a change in clinical practice; the ranking is a relevance-led snapshot rather than measured popularity.
